display.purpose: Page/section titles, brand mark, modal headings. Archivo, 700 weight.

body.purpose: Default text everywhere — dense information UI, smaller and tighter than an editorial site.

label.purpose: IDs, timestamps, stat numbers, version strings — anything generated or measured rather than written. Includes the Mono-Eyebrow (tracked uppercase section/readout labels, e.g. panel headers and KPI category labels) and Mono-KPI-Value (large KPI-tile numerics) sub-patterns — see DESIGN.md §3.

control.purpose: Interactive chrome (buttons, tabs, inputs, filter dropdowns) — the app's most common text size by volume, not a one-off.

shadows.name: sm
shadows.purpose: Barest lift — icon-button hover, small popovers. Dark mode: rgba(0,0,0,0.35).

shadows.name: md
shadows.purpose: Dropdowns, tooltips, small floating panels. Dark mode: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.4), 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.28).

shadows.name: lg
shadows.purpose: Modals — the only surface that reads as floating above everything else. Deepened in the Command Band re-skin to match the new chrome's modal depth. Dark mode: 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.5), 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.3) — unchanged from before.

shadows.name: drawer
shadows.purpose: Left nav drawer sliding over the page; chrome floats by definition.

motion.name: t-fast
motion.purpose: Default for color/background/border transitions on buttons, tabs, icon-buttons.

motion.name: t-med
motion.purpose: Slightly slower transitions where the fast token feels too abrupt (larger surfaces).

motion.name: drawer-slide
motion.purpose: Nav drawer open/close, the one slower move; entrance animations are disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Deep Navy CTA button — the content-area action color, distinct from the on-chrome Chrome Accent blue (see DESIGN.md §2, The CTA/Chrome Color Rule).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 30px; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: var(--r-md); border: 1px solid var(--primary); background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-fg); font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 500; transition: background var(--t-fast), border-color var(--t-fast); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--primary-hot); border-color: var(--primary-hot); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Default hairline-bordered button used for everything that isn't the primary action.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 30px; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: var(--r-md); border: 1px solid var(--line); background: var(--bg-elev); color: var(--fg); font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 500; transition: background var(--t-fast), border-color var(--t-fast); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--bg-subtle); border-color: var(--line-strong); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Icon Button
components.description: Square transparent icon button with an optional notification badge.
components.css: .ds-icon-btn { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 30px; height: 30px; padding: 0; border-radius: var(--r-md); border: 1px solid transparent; background: transparent; color: var(--fg-mute); transition: color var(--t-fast), background var(--t-fast), border-color var(--t-fast); } .ds-icon-btn:hover { color: var(--fg); background: var(--bg-subtle); border-color: var(--line); } .ds-icon-btn-badge { position: absolute; top: 2px; right: 2px; min-width: 15px; height: 15px; padding: 0 3px; border-radius: 10px; background: var(--err); color: #fff; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }

components.name: Input
components.description: Default text input with the Command Blue focus ring.
components.css: .ds-input { height: 30px; padding: 5px 10px; border-radius: var(--r-md); border: 1px solid var(--line); background: var(--bg-elev); color: var(--fg); font-size: 12.5px; transition: border-color var(--t-fast), box-shadow var(--t-fast); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--accent); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--accent-wash); }

components.name: Tabs
components.description: In-content sub-tab pair (Admin / Master Data / Gantt Timeline-Orders / Labor) — idle vs. active state, active marked by a Command Blue outline. The app's top-level nav itself now lives in the dark left drawer with its own Chrome Accent rail treatment (see DESIGN.md §5, Tabs).
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 2px; } .ds-tab-btn { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; height: 30px; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: var(--r-md); border: 1px solid transparent; background: transparent; color: var(--fg-mute); font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 500; transition: background var(--t-fast); } .ds-tab-btn:hover { color: var(--fg); background: var(--bg-subtle); } .ds-tab-btn--active { color: var(--fg); background: var(--bg-subtle); border-color: var(--line); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 0; }

components.name: Modal
components.description: Head/body/foot modal shell — the primary use of shadow-lg in the whole system.
components.html:
Edit Order
Modal content goes here.
components.css: .ds-modal { display: flex; flex-direction: column; width: 100%; max-width: 440px; max-height: 90vh; background: var(--bg-elev); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: var(--r-lg); box-shadow: var(--shadow-lg); font-family: 'Public Sans', sans-serif; } .ds-modal-head { padding: 14px 18px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); font-family: 'Archivo', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--fg); } .ds-modal-body { padding: 18px; overflow: auto; color: var(--fg); font-size: 13px; } .ds-modal-foot { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; gap: 8px; padding: 12px 18px; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); background: var(--bg-subtle); } .ds-modal-foot button { height: 30px; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: var(--r-md); font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 500; transition: background var(--t-fast), border-color var(--t-fast); } .ds-modal-foot button:first-child { border: 1px solid var(--line); background: var(--bg-elev); color: var(--fg); } .ds-modal-foot button:first-child:hover { background: var(--bg-subtle); border-color: var(--line-strong); } .ds-modal-foot button:last-child { border: 1px solid var(--primary); background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-fg); } .ds-modal-foot button:last-child:hover { background: var(--primary-hot); border-color: var(--primary-hot); }

components.name: Toast
components.css: .ds-toast { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: var(--r-md); color: #fff; font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 500; box-shadow: var(--shadow-md); } .ds-toast--success { background: var(--ok); } .ds-toast--error { background: var(--err); } .ds-toast--warn { background: var(--warn); } .ds-toast--info { background: var(--info); }

components.name: Badge
components.description: Soft-tint status label — distinct from the solid-fill toast.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: var(--r-sm); font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-badge--warn { background: var(--warn-soft); color: var(--warn); } .ds-badge--err { background: var(--err-soft); color: var(--err); } .ds-badge--info { background: var(--info-soft); color: var(--info); }

components.name: KPI Tile
components.description: Dashboard stat tile: mono eyebrow label, mono value, 3px colored top border for severity (the sanctioned stripe exception).
components.css: .ds-kpi { width: 160px; padding: 10px 12px; background: var(--bg-elev); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-top: 3px solid var(--fg-faint); border-radius: var(--r-lg); } .ds-kpi--warn { border-top-color: var(--warn); } .ds-kpi-k { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--fg-mute); } .ds-kpi-v { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 24px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: var(--fg); }

components.name: Update Banner
components.description: In-flow 34px advisory strip under the context bar announcing a newer build; info tint, never error red.
components.html: ⓘA newer version is available. Refresh to update.b138
components.css: .ds-update-banner { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; height: 34px; padding: 0 18px; background: var(--info-soft); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--info); color: var(--fg); font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-update-ico { color: var(--info); font-size: 13px; } .ds-update-msg { flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-update-build { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.02em; }

components.name: Stack-Count Badge
components.description: Pill on a Gantt machine label marking overlapping orders hidden in a collapsed row; solid when expanded.
components.css: .ds-stack { min-width: 28px; padding: 2px 7px; border: 0; border-radius: 10px; background: var(--err-soft); color: var(--err); font: inherit; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1; text-align: center; cursor: pointer; } .ds-stack:hover { filter: brightness(0.95); } .ds-stack:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-stack--open { background: var(--err); color: var(--bg-elev); }

components.name: Alert Monitor Row
components.description: One 44px alert line: severity glyph, mono prefix, message, mono when-column, hairline separator.
components.html: ⚠M-204Tool conflict with order 45012 days late
components.css: .ds-am-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 14px minmax(0,1fr) 140px; align-items: center; column-gap: 12px; padding: 0 12px; height: 44px; box-sizing: border-box; box-shadow: inset 0 -1px 0 var(--line); background: var(--bg-elev); } .ds-am-row:hover { background: var(--bg-subtle); } .ds-am-sev { color: var(--warn); font-size: 12px; text-align: center; } .ds-am-main { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; min-width: 0; } .ds-am-pfx { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 11px; color: var(--fg-mute); } .ds-am-msg { font-size: 13px; color: var(--fg); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-am-when { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 11px; color: var(--err); }

narrative.overview: NIMBUS is a control-room instrument, not a consumer app that happens to render a Gantt chart. The chrome is a permanently-dark navy command band and left drawer wrapping a cool gray-blue page of flat white cards, with a bright signal-blue accent for the on-chrome CTA and highlight — the visual grammar of a mission-control console, not a SaaS dashboard. Every surface is dense with real information (order counts, due dates, line utilization) because the people using it are experts scheduling production every day, not casual visitors who need to be onboarded gently. The system still separates regions with hairline borders by default and reserves shadows for genuinely floating surfaces (modals, popovers), but color now does more work than the old single-accent system: navy is chrome/structure, bright blue is the on-chrome highlight/CTA, and a darker navy fill is the CTA anywhere in the light content area (see the CTA/Chrome Color Rule). It rejects the same two failure modes as before — the bubbly, gradient-hero gloss of generic consumer SaaS, and the dated grid-of-forms clunkiness of legacy ERP screens. NIMBUS sits between them: modern craft applied to an industrial, information-dense tool.
keyCharacteristics: Navy chrome (command band + left drawer) fixed dark in both light/dark theme, wrapping a cool gray-blue content area
Bright blue is the on-chrome CTA/highlight; navy fill is the content-area CTA — two CTA colors doing two different jobs
Hairline borders and flat surfaces by default; shadows are the exception, now navy-tinted rather than warm-tinted
JetBrains Mono for anything numeric or machine-generated, including the Mono-Eyebrow label and Mono-KPI-Value patterns
Brisk, exact motion — nothing lingers, nothing bounces

rules.name: The CTA/Chrome Color Rule
rules.body: Navy is chrome/structure (command band, drawer, fixed dark in both themes). Bright blue (--chrome-accent) is the on-chrome highlight and the CTA that lives ON the band/drawer (e.g. Save). Content-area CTAs (.btn-primary, .seg-btn.active outside the chrome) are navy fill (--primary), not blue. --accent blue is for links, active-tab outlines, and focus rings in the light content area only, never a solid CTA fill there.

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule (retired)
rules.body: The old rule — a single accent color (Foundry Amber) that was never a background fill, only a line/outline/icon/focus ring — no longer holds. This re-skin intentionally introduces a second, filled CTA color (Deep Navy) and a chrome-scoped bright-blue CTA (Chrome Accent) alongside the outline-only accent. Kept here as a historical marker, not an active rule — see The CTA/Chrome Color Rule above for what replaced it.

rules.name: The Hairline-Over-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Regions are separated by a 1px border by default. A shadow is a deliberate signal that something is floating above the page (a modal, a popover), not a decorative default on every card.

rules.name: The Dark-Mode Remap, Not Reversal
rules.body: Dark mode re-lights the same navy/blue structure rather than inverting it: --accent brightens (#1f5fbf → #4d9fff) for legibility on a dark page, and --primary gets its own lighter navy (#12263f → #2b4f78) rather than reusing the light-mode value — so content-area CTAs still read as a distinct "action" color against a dark background (a change from the old system, where Deep Slate was literally the same hex in both themes). The --chrome-* tokens do not change between themes at all — the command band and drawer are fixed-dark chrome, a deliberate structural exception (see §4 Elevation). Every :root color token, including the bar-mode, zone and alert-cell groups and all the compatibility aliases, now has a body.dark counterpart (the horizon and elapsed-time washes keep their :root values by design). New CSS must add its dark value in the same change and use tokens only; check :root and body.dark in styles.css before assuming a token exists.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Machine Rule
rules.body: If a string was generated, measured, or timestamped rather than written by a person, it renders in JetBrains Mono. This is the fastest visual cue in the system for "this is data, not copy." The Mono-Eyebrow/Mono-KPI-Value pairing on every KPI tile is the most consistent, highest-visibility application of this rule today.

rules.name: The Floating-Means-Floating Rule
rules.body: A shadow above the sm step is reserved for something the user should read as temporarily suspended over the interface (a modal, an overlay). Don't reach for shadow-lg on a static panel just to make it feel "premium" — that's the legacy-ERP-meets-consumer-SaaS mistake this system explicitly avoids.

dos: Do follow the CTA/Chrome Color Rule: navy chrome, bright-blue on-chrome CTA/highlight, navy-fill content-area CTAs, blue outline/ring for links and focus in the content area — never mix the four up (§2).
Do separate regions with a 1px Hairline border by default; reach for a shadow only when something is genuinely floating above the page (modal, popover, splash card).

Do render anything generated/measured/timestamped in JetBrains Mono (IDs, durations, stat numbers, version strings) — including the Mono-Eyebrow label and Mono-KPI-Value numeric patterns now used throughout KPI tiles and panel headers (§3).
Do use a colored top-border for KPI/stat-tile severity (border-top: 3px solid var(--warn|--err)) — the one sanctioned exception to the no-colored-accent-stripe don't below (top-border, not side).
Do use Flatpickr for every date/time input — never native <input type="date">, datetime-local, or time (the one exception is the AG Grid inline date-cell editor).
Do use searchable/filterable comboboxes for plant and line selection, scoped to the plant→line hierarchy — this system is built to hold 50+ plants and 3,500+ lines, not the pilot's handful.
Do re-skin third-party components (vis-timeline, Flatpickr, AG Grid) to the token system rather than shipping their default look.
Do keep transitions fast (0.12–0.18s) and exponential-ease — a hover state should register like a mechanical switch, not a soft fade.
donts: Don't use bubble or chip selectors for plants or lines — they break down past ~10 entries and this system must scale to thousands.
Don't add gradient-hero sections, gradient text, or glassmorphism as a decorative default — that's the generic-consumer-SaaS gloss this system explicitly rejects.
Don't use dated grid-of-forms ERP layouts, oversized bordered table cells, or beige/gray corporate-form styling — that's the legacy-ERP clunk this system explicitly rejects.

Don't use border-left/border-right as a colored accent stripe on cards or list rows — full borders, background tints, or a leading icon instead. (The one sanctioned exception is the KPI-tile border-top severity pattern in §5 — top, not side, and only on .kpi-tile.)

Don't reference a CSS variable name that isn't defined in :root or body.dark without checking first, and don't add a :root color without its body.dark value. The compatibility aliases (--border, --border-subtle, --font-mono, --nimbus-amber/--amber, --bg-float, --surface, --text-muted) are all defined, but prefer the canonical token names in new CSS.
Don't use --warn as small text or an icon color on a light surface (~3.2:1); use --warn-text. --warn is for fills, borders and tints.
Don't add a status or category color outside Signal OK/Warn/Err/Info and the nine --pal-* swatches, and don't tint a Gantt bar by anything but firming status or the active profile's category color.
Don't reach for --shadow-lg on a static, non-floating panel just to make it feel more "premium" — see The Floating-Means-Floating Rule.
